title: The Eagle and the Arrow

full_text:
A majestic eagle soared high above the jagged mountain peaks, his great golden wings riding the thermals with regal ease. Looking down with keen, telescopic vision from the clouds, he surveyed the rocky crags, seeking hare or grouse among the boulders.

Down in the ravine, a solitary archer spotted the great bird circling against the blue sky. The hunter notched a slender wooden arrow onto his bowstring, drew the cord back to his ear, and released the shaft with a musical twang.

The arrow shot upward through the air like a whistling streak of lightning. It pierced the eagle's breast with mortal precision.

Folding his mighty wings in agony, the great monarch of the heavens tumbled from the sky, crashing down upon a carpet of mountain moss. As the eagle lay gasping his last breath, his dimming eyes looked down at the fatal shaft embedded deep in his chest.

To his bitter grief, he saw that the arrow's guiding fletching was made from one of his own dropped feathers, which the archer had plucked from the crags weeks before.

"Alas," groaned the dying monarch with a heavy sigh, "how doubly bitter is my end! It was not enough that man sought my life, but my own wings provided the feather that guided the fatal shaft straight to my heart!"
moral: It sharpens the sting of sorrow when we realize our own gifts furnished the weapon of our downfall.
